I-85 crash: 8 dead, multiple cats injured after semi-truck collision in Georgia
===============================================================================

The identity of the victims has not yet been publicly announced.

By[Mason Leath](https://abcnews.com/author/Mason_Leath)

October 14, 2025, 1:39 PM

![](https://i.abcnewsfe.com/a/993f56b3-9eb0-4359-9904-8c07f77a1070/REDACTED.jpg?w=992)

0:35

A fiery crash caused a chain reaction along I-85 in Jackson County, Georgia, Oct. 13, 2025.

WSB

Eight people were killed in a fiery, six-vehicle pileup on Interstate 85 in Jackson County, Georgia, the Jackson County Coroner's Office confirmed to ABC News.

A semi-trailer chicken feed truck collided into the back of a Dodge Grand Caravan on Monday afternoon, causing a chain reaction that ensnared four other cars in the northbound lanes of I-85, just south of mile marker 147, according to the Georgia State Patrol.

The Dodge van caught on fire and all seven passengers, including three adults and five children, were pronounced dead at the scene. All the victims were family members, according to officials.

The coroner confirmed to ABC News on Tuesday that another individual in the pile-up was also pronounced dead, bringing the death toll to eight.

The driver allegedly responsible, Kane Hammock, 33, was taken into custody and charged with eight counts of vehicular homicide, feticide, following too closely, no registration and failure to exercise due care.

He is from Gainesville, GA, according to authorities.

![](https://i.abcnewsfe.com/a/1c200db4-633c-4021-ad74-d5e4b326dc40/kane-hammock-main-ht-jt-251014_1760477791603_hpMain_4x3.jpg)

In this booking photo released by the Jackson County Sheriff's Office, Kane Hammock is shown.

Jackson County Sheriff's Office

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), in coordination with the Georgia State Patrol, has opened a safety investigation into this fatal crash.

Officials have not yet released the identities of those killed.

![](https://i.abcnewsfe.com/a/993f56b3-9eb0-4359-9904-8c07f77a1070/REDACTED.jpg)

A fiery crash caused a chain reaction along I-85 in Jackson County, Georgia, Oct. 13, 2025.

WSB

One of the vehicles in the crash was an animal transportation van that belonged to Furkids Animal Rescue and Shelters, Georgia's largest no-kill animal shelter, according to their website.

I-85 northbound lanes reopen after deadly crash involving tanker
================================================================

All northbound lanes on I-85 in DeKalb County reopened early Sunday after crews cleaned up a deadly crash involving a tanker truck.

By [Atlanta News First staff](/authors/atlantanewsfirststaff/)

Published: May 10, 2026 at 7:36 AM EDT|Updated: May 10, 2026 at 9:44 PM EDT

Share

[

Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google



](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=https://www.atlantanewsfirst.com)

ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) — All northbound lanes on I-85 in DeKalb County reopened early Sunday after crews cleaned up a fiery multi-vehicle crash that killed one person, according to police.

DeKalb County police officers initially responded around 1:20 a.m. to a traffic call on I-85 northbound near Shallowford Road involving a box truck and a Ford F-150. Investigators later determined the box truck was following too closely and rear-ended the F-150. After the collision, the box truck came to a controlled stop in the right lane and shoulder, and its driver fled the scene on foot.

![I-85 north was shut down for several hours early Sunday.](https://gray-wgcl-prod.gtv-cdn.com/resizer/v2/J35MJBANYRGM7AM4GUEZTPRZKE.png?auth=1c2bbec7a573afb0c4891b481ff43494bc267113e706b1145540371baa90b295&width=980&height=551&smart=true)

Tanker crashes on I-85 Northbound in DeKalb County.(Gray Media)

At approximately 2:11 a.m., GSP was dispatched to assist DeKalb County with the serious injury crash, which was blocking all northbound lanes. While DeKalb County police were blocking the right lane near the disabled vehicles, a Ford Excursion traveling in the second lane from the left struck the F-150, causing it to rotate into lane three. A semi-tanker traveling in lane three then collided with the F-150 and caught fire.

The driver of the F-150 was ejected from the vehicle and transported to Grady Memorial Hospital, where they were later pronounced dead.

Emergency crews worked for more than seven hours to clear the crash scene and reopen the interstate.

Results for the three pages. Two loaded, one returned 403.

1. 11Alive (https://www.11alive.com/article/news/local/1-dead-several-injured-in-fiery-crash-on-i-85-in-dekalb-county/85-2049afec-7776-4b9b-93e6-193440f9cb28): FAILED. HTTP 403 Forbidden, body not retrieved. This is a permanent failure, so sending the same URL again would fail the same way. No facts from this page.

2. Atlanta News First (https://www.atlantanewsfirst.com/2026/05/10/fiery-crash-involving-tanker-2-other-vehicles-closes-i-85-northbound-lanes/): loaded (HTTP 200). Page is from a non-preapproved source, so quotes are kept short.
- Date: Published May 10, 2026, 7:36 AM EDT; updated May 10, 2026, 9:44 PM EDT. Initial police response was "around 1:20 a.m." that day.
- Location: I-85 northbound near Shallowford Road, DeKalb County. Page does not give a direction beyond northbound, or a mile marker or exit number.
- Vehicles: box truck, Ford F-150, Ford Excursion, semi-tanker (the page's "semi-tanker"). The box truck rear-ended the F-150, the Excursion struck the F-150, and the semi-tanker then hit the F-150 and caught fire.
- Dead: one. "killed one person, according to police." The F-150 driver was ejected and taken to Grady Memorial Hospital, "where they were later pronounced dead."
- Injured: not stated.
- Other hospitals: none stated.
- Lane closure: all northbound lanes blocked. Page says all northbound lanes "reopened early Sunday." Also says "Emergency crews worked for more than seven hours to clear the crash scene and reopen the interstate." No exact closure start or end time.
- Source: "according to police" (DeKalb County police). Georgia State Patrol was also dispatched at about 2:11 a.m. to assist DeKalb County.
- Note: the box truck driver "fled the scene on foot."

3. ABC News (https://abcnews.com/US/85-crash-8-dead-multiple-cats-injured-after/story?id=126508641): loaded (HTTP 200). Page is from a non-preapproved source. This crash is in 2025, not 2026, and is a different incident from the other two pages.
- Date: Oct. 13, 2025 (Monday afternoon), per the page's photo caption and body text. Article dated October 14, 2025, 1:39 PM.
- Location: I-85 northbound lanes "just south of mile marker 147," Jackson County, Georgia. Page says Jackson County is "about 60 miles north of Atlanta." No exit or street named.
- Vehicles: a semi-trailer chicken feed truck hit the back of a Dodge Grand Caravan, then the chain reaction "ensnared four other cars." Six vehicles in total. The van was an animal transport van belonging to Furkids Animal Rescue and Shelters. It was carrying 37 cats to a shelter in Vermont.
- Dead: 8. "Eight people were killed," per the Jackson County Coroner's Office. Seven were pronounced dead at the scene (three adults and five children, all family members) and one more later, per the coroner.
- Injured: no human injury count stated. The page says "the driver, along with multiple cats, sustained injuries." Five cats are reported missing, citing Furkids' Facebook post.
- Hospitals: not stated.
- Lane closure: the page says the collision "closed all northbound lanes of I-85 in the area until almost 10 p.m."
- Source: Georgia State Patrol (spokesperson Franka Young, quoted), Jackson County Coroner's Office (confirmed the death toll to ABC News). NTSB opened a safety investigation with GSP.
- Driver: Kane Hammock, 33, of Gainesville, GA, was charged with eight counts of vehicular homicide, among other charges, per the page.
